openings.claim: Can removable edge stops retain the hatch under light seating, removing tight hatch-pressure dependence without merely relocating friction to an inadequately gripped rim?
openings.delta: Refine the prior bearing proposal: four supplied strips form two padded removable rim jaws, with inner edges registering the hatch. Distinguish hatch-to-stop bearing from jaw-to-rim grip. Cord recovers released parts; jaws must park entirely outside the marked opening. Only supplied strips may be drilled or cut.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: tighter hatch seating alone supplies sufficient friction. Bearing predicts light seating can satisfy displacement and pull requirements even when tighter left-corner seating produces opposite-corner lift. Rival predicts success depends on tighter seating. Lift is diagnostic, not an added acceptance threshold. Jaw slip defeats either configuration and cannot establish that hatch pressure is necessary.
openings.probe: Before fabrication, inspect whether rim geometry allows reversible jaw attachment, edge bearing, release and exterior parking with supplied stock. If feasible, use stock sequentially for tighter friction seating and light seating with stops. Each receives ten opening cycles and six closure/pull trials at cycles 1, 2, 4, 6, 9 and 10; disturb final closure with the right-contact card. Record marked-position displacement, jaw movement, corner lift, reopening time and visible tears. Twelve pulls total. Success requires within 1 mm after ten cycles, surviving 20 N and one-technician reopening within 30 seconds; disturbed closure retains every requirement except seal continuity. Defeat includes jaw slip, ineffective stops, outcome failure, tears, opening obstruction, unrecoverable parts or exceeding 90-minute fabrication/20-minute observation capacities. Stop if safe reversible assembly is unavailable.
assumptions: Rim access, strip stiffness, pad grip and release geometry are indispensable unknowns.
Supplied stock and observation time may not support both informative configurations; a stop cap supplies no feasibility evidence.

assessment: One decision-relevant refinement; hypothetical fabrication/probe only. No performance, resource availability or deployment is established.

lineage.reason: Separate edge bearing from rim-grip dependence and make control interpretation and resource uncertainty explicit.
